lead.headline: From December, your ChatGPT chats and Codex runs come out of the same pot
lead.summary: A new OpenAI help page says Plus, Pro and Business plans will share one usage allowance across ChatGPT and Codex starting in December, as the agentic Work features fold into the main ChatGPT app. Usage will be counted in tokens, so bigger models and harder tasks burn more of it; only Instant chat stays free of the meter. Combined usage and reset times will sit in Settings → Usage, and at the limit you wait, upgrade or buy credits. The page appeared on 31 October and OpenAI hasn't given an exact date yet. If you lean on Codex, heavy chatting will now eat into your coding budget.

news.headline: DeepSeek open-sources a research prototype of an always-on coding agent for one GitHub repo
news.summary: dsh-superagent (MIT) listens to GitHub, opens a work item when an allowed person asks, runs it in its own session and directory, and answers in the same thread, often with a PR. Its rule: take as little human attention as possible. Not production-ready, and it runs with full access as your OS user.

news.headline: Banks and retailers are shutting the door on personal AI agents like Meta's Muse
news.summary: JPMorgan, Schwab, Amazon, Kohl's and Neiman Marcus block outside agents, while Walmart just opened up to them. An audit of 51 big US retailers found 37 block shopping agents mostly by accident, through old anti-scraper rules, and none offers a way for a verified agent to finish a purchase.

news.headline: OpenAI plans a post-midterms PR push, and might rename data centres "AI compute campuses"
news.summary: Chief global affairs officer Chris Lehane told Axios the midterms are a trailer for 2028, when he expects AI to be the issue. Ideas on the list: AI "speed limits", a US role in global standards, and a friendlier name for the buildings communities keep fighting.

news.headline: Lifeline's Timo Ahopelto: Finland could produce a €100B startup within five years
news.summary: On Kauppalehti's Markkinaraati, Ahopelto called a Finnish hectocorn entirely possible, citing Oura as proof that growth is hard to predict. Startup community CEO Riikka Pakarinen bets on deep tech like space and quantum; Verda, a unicorn since its $189M round in September, came up as a candidate.

x_posts.name: Ethan Mollick
x_posts.text:
GPT-4 could do 4 minutes of independent work with a 50% chance of success.

Current models can do multiple weeks of work, and January 2026 is a reasonable cut-off for the moment agentic work started.

Large productivity impacts before that would mostly be confined to coding.
x_posts.why: A handy date for when agents stopped being a coding-only story.
